nodes.label: Gesture-gated toast audio
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-28 - s5-fix-startup-toast-chime [ses_f1a63f048ffeZyV1um630y2Oag].md:L00058] Therefore: **do NOT gate `playAudio` itself.** Gating it would suppress all 652 event-bound sounds in environments where the synthetic event never fires, and would churn a large number of existing tests. Gate the **toast cue** only.

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-28 - s5-fix-startup-toast-chime [ses_f1a63f048ffeZyV1um630y2Oag].md:L52] Many toasts are raised by background work, not by anything the user did, so any user without Ollama installed got an error chime every time the app launches, before touching anything.

nodes.label: vitest serves undeclared exports from a throwing Proxy, so a bare vi.mock factory breaks any runtime read of them
nodes.norm_label: vitest serves undeclared exports from a throwing proxy, so a bare vi.mock factory breaks any runtime read of them
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-28 - s5-fix-startup-toast-chime [ses_f1a63f048ffeZyV1um630y2Oag].md:L06128] `utils/audio` is mocked in 161 test files and vitest serves undeclared exports from a throwing Proxy, so reading a new `hasUserInteracted()` from it would make the negative control fail **by design**, and the task forbids weakening that test.

nodes.label: Negative control test
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-28 - s5-fix-startup-toast-chime [ses_f1a63f048ffeZyV1um630y2Oag].md:L06130] Its `beforeEach` now does `resetToastInteractionForTests()` (order independence) plus a real `window.dispatchEvent(new Event("pointerdown"))` that reaches the actual capture-phase listener, while the audio mock still offers only `playAudio`.

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-28 - s5-fix-startup-toast-chime [ses_f1a63f048ffeZyV1um630y2Oag].md:L6191] The reason for the literal table is kept and is now accurate: undeclared exports throw from vitest's Proxy, that caused 14 real failures, and the single remaining bare factory is the standing negative control.

nodes.label: The user-interaction latch lives in ToastSound.tsx, not utils/audio.ts
nodes.norm_label: the user-interaction latch lives in toastsound.tsx, not utils/audio.ts
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-28 - s5-fix-startup-toast-chime [ses_f1a63f048ffeZyV1um630y2Oag].md:L06128] Keeping the latch in `ToastSound.tsx` means the toast path reads exactly one thing from `utils/audio` (`playAudio`), before and after the change, so the negative control needed no structural rescue at all. It is also the more honest location: this is a toast-cue rule, not a general audio rule, and putting it in `utils/audio` would invite a future reader to think it applies to `playAudio`.

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-28 - s5-fix-startup-toast-chime [ses_f1a63f048ffeZyV1um630y2Oag].md:L2376] The recommendation was utils/audio.ts, but the negative control is a hard constraint, so the state was placed where the bare factory cannot observe it.

nodes.label: Capture-phase, passive, module-load interaction listener
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-28 - s5-fix-startup-toast-chime [ses_f1a63f048ffeZyV1um630y2Oag].md:L6132] Registered at module load, not in an effect, so the latch is armed before the first background toast can fire. Capture matters: a bubble-phase handler calling stopPropagation() must not be able to raise a toast before the latch flips. touchstart is kept because a webview that has not synthesised pointer events still delivers it, and it is idempotent otherwise.

nodes.label: The AppImage branch of PCSX2's DataRoot logic overrides portable.txt, and -datapath appends a literal 'PCSX2'
nodes.norm_label: the appimage branch of pcsx2's dataroot logic overrides portable.txt, and -datapath appends a literal 'pcsx2'
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - setup-game-ps2-dari-folder-games [ses_f163a11ebffeOc1sDO0LmUW6lt].md:L7044] -portable is useless on an AppImage. Pcsx2Config.cpp:2258-2271 checks getenv('APPIMAGE') first and, if it is set, forces DataRoot to <AppImage dir>/PCSX2, ignoring the contents of portable.txt entirely. The portable.txt already sitting in the folder becomes dead.

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - setup-game-ps2-dari-folder-games [ses_f163a11ebffeOc1sDO0LmUW6lt].md:L3071] -datapath is also unusable here: it does Path::Combine(CustomDataPath, 'PCSX2'), appending the literal string, so -datapath /home/.../Games/PS2 yields DataRoot /home/.../Games/PS2/PCSX2 rather than the folder itself.

nodes.label: Symlink ~/.config/PCSX2 to the existing folder so it becomes the emulator's DataRoot
nodes.norm_label: symlink ~/.config/pcsx2 to the existing folder so it becomes the emulator's dataroot
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - setup-game-ps2-dari-folder-games [ses_f163a11ebffeOc1sDO0LmUW6lt].md:L7046] What does work is the symlink: Path::RealPath on Linux resolves symlinks per component (FileSystem.cpp:388-425), so ~/.config/PCSX2 reads as ~/Games/PS2. Proof in the log: DataRoot Directory: /home/belajarcarabelajar/Games/PS2.

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - setup-game-ps2-dari-folder-games [ses_f163a11ebffeOc1sDO0LmUW6lt].md:L03572] Confirmed: Path::RealPath on Linux resolves symlinks and works on non-existent paths, doing an lstat per component and stopping the existence check after the first error while still building the path.

nodes.label: A PCSX2 .ps2 memory card file is 16384 sectors of 528 bytes, mapped 1:1 onto card address
nodes.norm_label: a pcsx2 .ps2 memory card file is 16384 sectors of 528 bytes, mapped 1:1 onto card address
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - setup-game-ps2-dari-folder-games [ses_f163a11ebffeOc1sDO0LmUW6lt].md:L09532] **Card size**: `McdSizeInSectors = m_fileSize / (SectorSize + EraseBlockSizeInSectors)` = 8650752 / (512 + 16) = 8650752 / 528 = 16384.

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - setup-game-ps2-dari-folder-games [ses_f163a11ebffeOc1sDO0LmUW6lt].md:L9610] Seek is a raw FSeek64(f, adr, SEEK_SET), so card address equals file offset 1:1, with no header offset. The 512-byte assumption was what made the first two integrity tests wrong.

nodes.label: PCSX2 never writes per-sector checksums into a .ps2 memory card file; the bytes stay at the 0xFF fill
nodes.norm_label: pcsx2 never writes per-sector checksums into a .ps2 memory card file; the bytes stay at the 0xff fill
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - setup-game-ps2-dari-folder-games [ses_f163a11ebffeOc1sDO0LmUW6lt].md:L09780] The per-sector XOR checksum is simply not present in PCSX2's file format. The checksum bytes are 0xFF, the fill value from Create(), never updated, and the guest BIOS computes checksums on the fly during transfer rather than reading them from the file.

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - setup-game-ps2-dari-folder-games [ses_f163a11ebffeOc1sDO0LmUW6lt].md:L9845] So a checksum audit of a .ps2 file measures something PCSX2 never writes; the 'tousands of sectors differ' number is void, not evidence of damage.

nodes.label: The PS1 memory card checksum formula does not apply to PS2 cards
nodes.norm_label: the ps1 memory card checksum formula does not apply to ps2 cards
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - setup-game-ps2-dari-folder-games [ses_f163a11ebffeOc1sDO0LmUW6lt].md:L09039] This checksum test is invalid. The formula at MemoryCardProtocol.cpp:118 lives inside the ps1McState block, which is PS1 memory card support, not the PS2 card. My conclusion that 16313 sectors were corrupt was a false alarm from a wrong method.

nodes.label: 'Formatted' in the PCSX2 log is a 26-byte header string compare, not an integrity check
nodes.norm_label: 'formatted' in the pcsx2 log is a 26-byte header string compare, not an integrity check
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - setup-game-ps2-dari-folder-games [ses_f163a11ebffeOc1sDO0LmUW6lt].md:L8437] FileMcd_IsMemoryCardFormatted (MemoryCardFile.cpp:873-889) only compares a 26 byte header against the string 'Sony PS2 Memory Card Format'. It does not verify the directory table, block allocation, or checksum integrity, so 'Formatted' in the log is a very weak check and does not mean healthy.

nodes.label: PCSX2 memory card FAT entries are indexed relative to alloc_offset, not absolutely
nodes.norm_label: pcsx2 memory card fat entries are indexed relative to alloc_offset, not absolutely
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - setup-game-ps2-dari-folder-games [ses_f163a11ebffeOc1sDO0LmUW6lt].md:L14387] The root cause: I indexed the FAT table entries by absolute cluster number when they are relative to alloc_offset. I tested three predicted FAT numbers and all three were right; the 483-plus-terminator figure I had been holding was a different data region's chain that happened to be neatly sequential.

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - setup-game-ps2-dari-folder-games [ses_f163a11ebffeOc1sDO0LmUW6lt].md:L14388] With the correct indexing, 22 real files (19 in slot 1, 3 in slot 2) were checked one by one and every length matched its chain exactly (524/524, 949/949, 992/992, 100/100, 63/63), all terminators valid, all consecutive. Zero problems.
